name: photo-grading-skill
role: photo color grading / photo color correction execution (processing); deterministic measurement and optimization against a caller-supplied target; not decision, not automatic look/LUT selection
description: Deterministic photo color grading: 3-way color grading wheels (teal & orange, warm & cool, any hue/saturation palette), typed photo corrections (white balance, exposure, contrast, levels, vibrance, sharpness), 3D LUT application, and an OKLab critic/optimizer that scores against a caller-supplied target - executed as typed, validated, deterministic operations through FFmpeg, with output validation and provenance. Not an AI agent: it never decides which look to apply, nor which correction values to use.
not_provided: automatic white balance (WHITE_BALANCE takes explicit temperature/tint values)
automatic color correction guesswork (no auto exposure/contrast/white balance)

tools.description: Execute a typed photo project and write a validated photo with provenance
tools.idempotency_hint: content_equivalent; intermediates reused by deterministic operation id
tools.verification: every artifact is re-probed: photo stream exists, width/height unchanged from the source (tolerance 1px), readable; measured signalstats of the input and output recorded as OBSERVED values in provenance
tools.execution: local subprocess: `ffmpeg -nostdin -y -i <photo> -vf <filters> <out>` / `ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <photo>` / `ffmpeg -i <photo> -vf signalstats -f null -`; no shell, no network, no user-supplied filter strings (values reaching argv are fixed flags or paths this skill resolved itself)

operations.description: Pass-through measurement op: re-encodes the input losslessly and attaches an OKLab `report` (median L, p05-p95 spread, clipping, near-neutral cast, Hasler-Suesstrunk M3 colourfulness, shadow/highlight tint hue+magnitude, skin-hue shift, mean OKLab distance). It changes no pixels and decides no look.

max_pixels.description: pixels sampled from the full image for analysis (stride, no resize)

operations.description: Typed photo corrections: white balance (temperature 2500-10000, tint -100..100), exposure (-10..10), contrast (-100..100), highlights/shadows/blacks/whites (-100..100), saturation (-100..100), vibrance (-100..100, weighted toward muted pixels), sharpness (0..100), clarity (0..100, local contrast), grain (0..50), chroma_denoise (0..100, chroma-only), and tone-curve anchors. Executed via ffmpeg eq/unsharp/cas/noise/hqdn3d plus generated LUTs for white balance and tonal bands.

Apply the 3-way Color Grading wheels (Shadows / Midtones / Highlights + Global): each wheel tints its tonal zone with a hue and saturation, plus zone luminance; `blending` mixes the tinted LUT back to identity, `balance` moves the zone boundaries. Executed by generating a 3D .cube LUT and applying it with ffmpeg lut3d. The classic cinematic look is teal shadows + orange highlights.

Per-hue-family HSL tweaks (red/orange/yellow/green/cyan/blue/magenta): hue/saturation/luminance shifts of the pixels in each family, executed via a generated LUT (buildlut.build_hsl_lut) with ffmpeg lut3d.

operations.description: Apply a 3D .cube LUT with ffmpeg lut3d. LUT is data read from disk, never a filter string.

lut_path.description: Path to a .cube LUT file (3D, <=10 MiB)

strength.description: Scale the LUT toward identity: 1 = full application, 0 = none

operations.description: Deterministic coordinate descent of the 8 grade parameters against the caller-supplied target, scored on a ~384 px proxy. The winner is baked into a 3D .cube LUT, applied to the proxy with numpy trilinear interpolation (matching ffmpeg lut3d), then rendered once at full size through lut3d. Accepted steps only; the result is never worse than the untouched image, and the full render is re-checked with an identity-LUT fallback. Requires the optional `critic` extra (numpy, Pillow).

highlight_hue.description: OKLab hue angle of the highlight tint (orange ~55)

tint_mag.description: OKLab chroma added in each zone (0.02-0.05 is a normal split tone)

colorfulness.description: Hasler-Suesstrunk M3 target (30 clinical, 45 average, 60+ punchy)

median_L.description: target median OKLab L (0.45-0.65 is a normal photo)

target.description: caller-supplied target look; every field is a number, no look names

proxy_size.description: longest side of the proxy the loop scores

lut_size.description: points per axis of the generated .cube LUT; 33 is the default, 65 if the 33^3 score is materially low

operations.description: Pass-through measurement op: PHOTO_ANALYZE plus a caller-supplied target look (six numbers) and a 0..100 score with every penalty term listed (exposure, contrast, clipping, colourfulness, shadow/highlight tint hue, tint strength, skin shift, overcooked guard). The target is data; the skill never chooses it.

provenance.identity: sha256 over canonical JSON of {type, parameters, input_identity (sha256 of the file), tool_versions}; no timestamps, no UUIDs; the LUT's sha256 (not path) is used for LUT ops
provenance.philosophy: measured values are OBSERVED and reported, never judged

highlight_hue.description: OKLab hue angle of the highlight tint (orange ~55)

target.note: All six fields are required numbers. Hue is an OKLab hue angle (0=red, 90=yellow, 180=green, 270=blue); teal ~200, orange ~55. A target is data supplied by the caller; there are no look presets.

critic.score: 100 + sum(penalties); each part reports penalty, measured value, target and tolerance. The score measures distance to the stated look without breaking constraints, not 'how good' a grade is.

optimizer.method: deterministic coordinate descent with a shrinking step; no RNG; accepted steps only
optimizer.guarantee: never worse than the untouched image: the optimizer accepts only improvements, the LUT path is re-scored, and the full render is re-checked with an identity-LUT fallback
